meeting_header:
Date: 2026-06-18 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Veridian - Head of ML), Ethan Ross (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Security), Jonas Blake (Product)
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on selecting between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. Key constraints: strict data residency in EU, SOC2 and customer-managed KMS desired, target p95 latency ~250ms for 512-token completions, expected 100-200 concurrent users peak (~30 QPS steady), cost sensitivity for inference at scale. Agreed next steps: exchange workload traces, run benchmark, share security docs, finalize success criteria and pilot timeline.
topics: Benchmark plan (throughput, p95, cold start, kv/prefix cache)
Deployment decision criteria: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Maya (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
00:08 Sara: Hi, Sara Patel here, Head of ML at Veridian. we run analytics pipelines and want to add a generative layer for reports.
00:15 Ethan: Ethan Ross, platform engineering, i'll be driving the infra side.
00:20 Priya: Priya, security/compliance. i'll vet the security artifacts.
00:26 Maya: Great, Liam our SE will kick through sizing and benchmarks.
00:30 Liam (SE): Hey all, thanks. high level, we want to understand your workload shape — tokens per request, concurrency, peak qps, and success criteria. can you share your SLOs?
00:44 Sara: Our soft target is p95 latency under 250ms for ~512 token generations, accuracy within our in-house evals (no regressions >2%), and unit cost below our threshold — ideally less than $X per 1M tokens.
01:02 Ethan: On load, typical steady qps is ~30, peaks to 50-60 for short bursts. concurrency about 100-200 users hitting interactive UI. batch jobs exist but are low priority.
01:18 Liam: ok that profile maps to three deployment options: Hosted (fastest to try, less ops), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput), Private (VPC or on-prem for strict controls). pros/cons matter for data residency and KMS.
01:34 Maya: question for Priya — do you need customer-managed key material (HSM/KMS), or is provider KMS ok?
01:41 Priya: We need customer-managed KMS for production and audit logs that include token-level traces redacted. also data must stay in EU region for certain datasets.
01:52 Liam: noted. Hosted can support region pins and bring-your-own-KMS in some cases but Dedicated / Private give stronger isolation and SLA guarantees. There are cost tradeoffs.
02:06 Sara: We're also worried about latency variance with multi-tenant hosting, especially for interactive UI. can you guarantee p95?
02:15 Liam: On hosted, we expose performance profiles — usually p95 fits but dedicated with reserved capacity reduces variance. private gives full control but adds ops overhead.
02:26 Ethan: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
02:30 Liam: sample request traces (timestamps, tokens per request), a set of 50-100 representative prompts, and target SLOs. we'll run throughput tests (qps), latency distributions, and regression tests versus your eval set.
02:45 Maya: we'll also provide a benchmark harness and script. expect cold-start and steady-state runs, and a KV/prefix cache test (since many of your prompts will share prefixes).
03:00 Jonas: side question — any fidelity differences with quantized models? we care about output quality.
03:07 Liam: quantization can reduce cost but may slightly change output. part of the POC is measuring quality vs cost — we'll run the same evals on different quantization profiles.
03:18 Priya: compliance: SOC2 docs, SAML/SSO support, RBAC, audit logs, and the KMS integration are must-haves. also data retention policies.
03:30 Maya: we'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO, penetration test summaries) and KMS integration docs after the call.
03:36 Sara: timeline — we want a quick pilot. what's realistic?
03:40 Maya: typical path: 2-week smoke + 4-week pilot with benchmarks, so 6 weeks to evaluate. if Dedicated or Private, provisioning adds 1-2 weeks.
03:51 Ethan: ok can we get pricing for all three modes?
03:54 Maya: yes, we'll share pricing bands: hosted per-token, dedicated as reserved capacity with commit levels, private as license + support + infra estimate.
04:06 Liam: for success criteria draft: p95 latency <250ms (512 tokens), throughput sustain 30 qps with headroom for 50, accuracy within 2% of baseline evals, cost per 1M tokens < $X, and security checklist items met.
04:29 Sara: that sounds right, maybe allow latency fallback to 350ms for some non-critical flows.
04:34 Liam: noted — we'll include tiers in the success doc.
04:39 Priya: on audit logs, we need token-level redaction and ability to export logs to our SIEM. is that supported?
04:46 Maya: yes, audit exports and integrations are supported, we'll include specifics.
04:52 Ethan: for benchmarks, can you simulate the UI traffic pattern? we have spiky bursts during reports generation.
04:58 Liam: yes, we'll parameterize the harness to reproduce bursty traffic. we can run a synthetic 1-hour soak to look at tail latencies.
05:10 Sara: any hard vendor lock-in? we want to keep portability.
05:15 Maya: Redwood supports model and config portability; Dedicated and Private give you more control over model versions and rollouts. Hosted is easiest to start but you can always migrate.
05:26 Jonas: procurement questions — what about contract length for Dedicated?
05:30 Maya: typically monthly or annual reserved capacity commitments; we'll give sample terms.
05:36 Priya: if we do Private on-prem, how much ops work is expected?
05:40 Liam: Private requires some infra work — networking (VPC peering), KMS/HSM setup, and on-prem packaging. we provide a deployment runbook and can do an install assist.
05:50 Sara: are there benchmark examples you can share?
05:53 Liam: yes, we'll send past benchmark reports (anonymized) and a spreadsheet template — link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/va-template (placeholder).
06:02 Maya: ok recap: we'll share runbook, pricing, security docs; Veridian sends traces and requirements; schedule benchmark run next week.
06:12 Ethan: i'll send traces by Monday.
06:15 Priya: i'll compile compliance list.
06:18 Sara: i'll review success criteria doc once you draft it.
06:22 Maya: great, we'll set up the benchmark and a follow-up on 2026-06-25. thanks all.
06:28 [call ends]
